Bug_Title: Regex boundaries should not be used in a way that can never be matched
Bug_Details:
In regular expressions the boundaries ^ and \A can only match at the beginning of the input (or, in case of ^ in combination with the MULTILINE flag, the beginning of the line) and $ , \Z and \z only at the end.
These patterns can be misused, by accidentally switching ^ and $ for example, to create a pattern that can never
match.
Noncompliant code example
// This can never match because $ and ^ have been switched around
Pattern.compile("$[a-z]+^"); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
Pattern.compile("^[a-z]+$");
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the regular expression pattern. The '$' is used at the start of the pattern and '^' is used at the end, which is incorrect. A regular expression can never match when start and end are switched.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case uses the showBug method with the input 'abc'. This input is a simple string of lowercase letters, but the regex pattern in the showBug method includes the '$' at the start and '^' at the end, which is incorrect. Hence, the assertFalse statement fails, triggering the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test result asserted that the'showBug' method correctly returned false for the input string 'abc'. This is expected behavior because the regular expression pattern '$[a-z]+^' is a non-matching pattern that can never match any input string, as per the bug information provided. Since the test did not produce any unexpected results, it can be inferred that the bug was not triggered.
